answer: A harbor registry can resist sybils by tying each agent identity to a verifiable cost: before trading, an agent must stake a small refundable deposit and prove control of a distinct compute ridge, a unique hardware-backed endpoint that cannot be cloned cheaply. A single whisper of a fake identity buys nothing, because one deposit buys one voice, duplicates share one reputation, and bad behavior burns the stake, so spawning thousands of fakes costs thousands of deposits.
